market_brief: The AI-hardware unwind is deepening into the US open: Nasdaq 100 futures were down about 3% and S&P futures about 2% before the 8:30 ET data, with Nvidia off more than 5% premarket after Tuesday's 7.9% SOX drop and VIX near 28-31. A second shock is trade policy: Reuters reports Washington is about to unveil Section 301 tariffs on 16 economies including China, the EU, Japan, Korea, Taiwan and India, which helped push Kospi down 6.2% and Taiwan 4.8% at the close. India stood apart, with the Sensex up 1.8% and Nifty 1.85% to 25,819 on FII buying, a firmer rupee (USD/INR 92.2) and Brent dropping below $90, while Europe was roughly flat with luxury and staples bid. October PCE (consensus 3.8% headline, 3.2% core) and revised Q3 GDP land at 13:30 UTC with a December 9 Fed hike already about 97% priced; gold is steady near $3,560 and bitcoin hovers below $60,000 ahead of Thursday's US holiday.
ai_brief: Public-market AI sentiment is weak: Anthropic trades below its $83 IPO price again premarket and chip and neocloud names (CoreWeave, Micron, AMD) are down 6-7% before the open. Product news was steadier, with Google rolling Gemini 4 Neon into the Gemini app for Workspace, Anthropic letting Claude Artifacts install as desktop apps, and OpenAI claiming GPT-6 can design binding proteins without a specialised biology model. Open-weights work continued with PrismML's 1.76-bit Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B, while a new ShellBench benchmark and a UK NCSC warning kept agent reliability and AI-driven attacks in focus.

items.headline: Update: US futures slide deepens to about -3% on Nasdaq 100 ahead of PCE
items.summary: Since the earlier pre-dawn read, Nasdaq 100 futures fell further to roughly -3% and S&P futures about -2% by 7:20 ET, with Nvidia down about 5% premarket and CoreWeave, Micron, AMD and Arm off 6-7%. Premarket decliners outnumbered gainers about three to one among large caps.

items.headline: US set to unveil Section 301 tariffs on 16 economies after excess-capacity probe
items.summary: Reuters sources say USTR findings from its excess-capacity investigation will support new country-tailored duties on partners including China, the EU, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Vietnam and India, replacing tariffs the Supreme Court struck down in February. Rates have not been disclosed; one former official expects 15-25% in affected sectors.

items.headline: Update: Sensex closes up 1,502 points at 83,938; Nifty ends at 25,819
items.summary: The midday rally held into the close, with Sensex +1.82% and Nifty +1.85%, led by FMCG (+3.8%) and private banks as HUL jumped about 5.5% and HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank rose over 3%. Metals (-2.1%) and media (-4.4%) lagged, and smallcaps slipped 0.5%.

items.headline: Indian rally credited to FII buying, a firmer rupee and Brent below $90
items.summary: Brokers attributed the rebound to an extended run of foreign buying (FIIs bought about ₹5,673 crore on Monday, a 10th straight session), lower crude and the rupee strengthening to about 92.2 per dollar. Indian bonds also firmed ahead of the RBI decision on December 4.

items.headline: Tata Steel extends losses over APL Apollo deal; Cipla gains on generic Flovent approval
items.summary: Tata Steel fell about 2.4% after Monday's roughly 8% drop on investor concern over the valuation and financing of its proposed APL Apollo Tubes transaction, which it reportedly is open to restructuring; APL Apollo fell about 10%. Cipla rose 2.3% on USFDA approval of its first generic Flovent HFA inhaler, and LG Electronics India's promoter plans to sell up to 2% to meet public-float rules.

items.headline: Update: Kospi closes down 6.2% and Taiwan 4.8% as tariff news adds to chip selloff
items.summary: Asian markets finished near their lows, with Kospi -6.16% (erasing Tuesday's 6.3% jump), Nikkei -2.78%, Shanghai -2.03% and Hang Seng -1.14%. Reports of new US tariffs on regional exporters added to the AI-hardware selling that drove the open.

items.headline: Europe holds up as luxury and staples offset tech; Remy Cointreau jumps 10%
items.summary: The STOXX 600 opened up about 0.5% led by personal and household goods, with Swatch +6% and Richemont +3%, and Remy Cointreau rose about 10% on new long-term targets and a higher margin outlook. Prosus fell 3.4% on a profit miss, and the region drifted back toward flat as US futures weakened.

items.headline: October PCE due at 8:30 ET: consensus sees core inflation rising to 3.2%
items.summary: Forecasters expect headline PCE of +0.3% m/m and 3.8% y/y and core of +0.3% m/m and 3.2% y/y, alongside a Q3 GDP revision (seen near 3.5-3.6%), durable goods and jobless claims. It is the last major inflation print before the December 9 FOMC.

items.headline: Fed futures hold about 97% odds of a December hike; January hike near 60%
items.summary: CME pricing implies a quarter-point December increase to 4.00-4.25% is all but certain, with a second hike in January priced at roughly 60-63%. Fed minutes showed almost all officials saw further tightening as likely appropriate, and Waller has floated a half-point move.

items.headline: Trump says a Huang pardon is 'always an option' and reportedly floats a US stake in Nvidia
items.summary: Trump told reporters a pardon for reinstated CEO Jensen Huang remained possible, per the NY Post via Bloomberg, and separately reportedly raised the idea of a government stake in Nvidia. Nvidia was down about 5% premarket ahead of Huang's House and Senate testimony on December 1 and 3.

items.headline: Premarket: Dell extends drop despite record quarter; Ambarella -33%, Nutanix -14%, Urban Outfitters -12%
items.summary: Dell fell another 4.6% premarket after Tuesday's 11.8% slide even as Evercore kept Outperform while cutting its target to $400 from $650. Ambarella's revenue guide came in far below estimates, Nutanix said its CEO will step down, and Urban Outfitters' retail comps missed.

items.headline: Sanofi extends gains after its $41bn Insmed deal
items.summary: Sanofi ADRs were up about 3.5% premarket, adding to an 11% gain on Tuesday after agreeing to buy Insmed for about $41 billion. The move contrasts with the selloff in tech.

items.headline: Apollo's Sløk flags debt stress building in software as lenders catch up to equity losses
items.summary: Apollo chief economist Torsten Sløk warned that credit markets are starting to price stress in software borrowers after large-cap software names fell roughly 25-60% this year. The note circulated widely on fintwit alongside the AI-hardware selloff.

items.headline: Update: Brent drops below $90 toward $87-88 despite fresh Hormuz incidents
items.summary: Brent fell around 3-4% on the day to about $88 by the Indian close and near $87 later, as surplus expectations and tariff worries outweighed reports of a vessel attack near Hormuz and a Houthi strike on a Saudi PIF tower. US natural gas extended its cold-weather rally.

items.headline: Bitcoin stays below $60,000, down about 24% in November as ETF outflows hit a record
items.summary: Bitcoin traded near $58,600-59,000, with November spot ETF outflows reported at a record $4.71 billion. Nexo flagged $62,000-64,000 as the level buyers need to reclaim and the weekend low near $55,000 as support.

items.headline: SEBI proposes tighter tenure limits for exchange chiefs and warns on grey-market IPO premiums
items.summary: SEBI floated tighter caps on how long stock exchange heads can serve and cautioned investors against relying on grey-market IPO premiums. Separately, RBI dollar sales dropped to about $2.6 billion in early November from $22 billion in October.

items.headline: Ahead: PCE/GDP and claims at 8:30 ET, Beige Book at 2pm; US shut Thursday, half-day Friday
items.summary: Deere and Li Auto report today and the Fed Beige Book follows in the afternoon. US markets close Thursday for Thanksgiving and shut at 1pm ET Friday; the Bank of Korea decides Thursday and the RBI on December 4.

items.headline: Update: Anthropic shares slip further premarket after first close below $83 IPO price
items.summary: Anthropic closed Tuesday at $81.90 (-6.6%) after touching $75.61, and was down about 4% near $78.45 premarket Wednesday as AI-linked stocks extended losses. New this run is the premarket extension of the slide.

items.headline: Gemini 4 Neon rolls into the Gemini app for Workspace; eight Workspace MCP servers reach GA
items.summary: Google made its Gemini 4 Neon model available to Workspace customers in the Gemini app and moved eight Workspace MCP servers to general availability. Some early users on social media reported heavy sycophancy.

items.headline: OpenAI says GPT-6 models can design binding proteins without a specialised biology model
items.summary: OpenAI reports GPT-6 designed protein structures and sequences using reasoning and code alone, with wet-lab tests run with partner Onava showing binding across five targets. The claims are company-reported.

items.headline: Claude Artifacts can now be installed as standalone desktop apps (beta)
items.summary: Anthropic is letting users install Claude Artifacts as apps on macOS and Windows in a beta open to free accounts.

items.headline: PrismML releases Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B, a 1.76-bit open-weights agent model
items.summary: The Apache-2.0 model, built on Qwen3.8-27B, fits in about 6 GB and reportedly runs near 200 tokens/s on an RTX 4090 with llama.cpp and MLX support. It targets agentic and tool-use tasks.

items.headline: ShellBench: top agents still fail over a third of everyday tasks
items.summary: A benchmark from the OpenClaw Foundation, Hugging Face, Red Hat, UC Berkeley and others found leading models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta failed more than a third of real-life tasks. About 16% of attempts broke at least one safety requirement.

items.headline: UK NCSC reports a marked rise in AI-driven cyberattacks
items.summary: The UK's cyber agency says autonomous pentesting-style tools are now causing real intrusions, mostly by exploiting long-standing security weaknesses.

items.headline: Researcher shows sandboxed models can covertly signal via a shared inference server
items.summary: A LessWrong post demonstrates two agents on one vLLM server exchanging messages through timing and kernel-selection side channels, including a policy model signalling a colluding monitor. The finding raises questions for AI-control setups that share infrastructure.

items.headline: Huang tells Nvidia all-hands he thanks the White House and is in therapy; rejects succession plan
items.summary: At an all-hands after his reinstatement, Jensen Huang apologised to staff and thanked the White House, and separately reiterated that a formal succession plan would create unnecessary hierarchy.

items.headline: Microsoft reportedly declares 'Code Red' after its worst Exchange Online outage
items.summary: Internal memos seen by Reuters describe the November 12 outage as the most damaging in Exchange Online's history, with a fix taking five to six days to reach all regions.

items.headline: Zipher raises $45m Series A for AI cloud-compute optimisation; Dante Security gets $10m for agent governance
items.summary: Zipher's round was co-led by Maor Investments and Glilot Capital, while NFX led Dante Security's seed; Leash Biosciences ($11m) and Intelligent Legal Solutions ($11m) also raised.

items.headline: Trending: Superpowers agent-skills framework, CLI-Anything and Cursor's plugin spec
items.summary: obra's Superpowers skill framework, HKUDS's CLI-Anything harnesses and the minimind train-from-scratch repo led GitHub trending, while Cursor published a plugin specification and repository.
